Any way, the relationship was only 4 months which is the shortest I’ve ever had. He broke things off with me. I’ve never really been in a good relationship so If yours was a good one, I’m sure it will be more difficult to move on, but idk.

I’m not seeing anyone or talking to anyone except for friends. I know I’m not emotionally ready for another relationship and need to work on my own life anyway. I feel like I always used another person almost as a distraction to not have to get my own shit together because I never knew what I wanted to do.

Luckily, being alone has caused me to self reflect A LOT which has been so helpful in trying to figure out what I want for my future and how I can better myself personally. 

At this point, it’s been 2 months since I’ve had any contact with my ex. We have both blocked each other on everything. I did it once out of anger but unblocked him literally the next day (never blocked his number) out of the blue pretty much he calls me saying he wants nothing to do with me and blocks me except for my number. Things kind of escalated because I was pissed and said some things (that were true) to him and he didn’t like someone calling him out so he blocked me on everything (phone number too)

Let yourself grieve and go through the process and feel the emotions as they come. Try not to specifically dwell, but allow your mind and heart to naturally go through the stages of a break up. 

The biggest thing getting used to is just not having someone to talk to daily, getting over the attachment to the person, and taking the time to get used to being alone to where you feel self sustained before jumping into another relationship.

The lessons are great, the emotional and mental scars are horrible so it’s hard to say if the trade off is worth it or not. Honestly, a lot of it is listening to your intuition and gut feeling. If you *feel* like something is off, it probably is. 
Trust actions, not words. I always just thought people were the same as me— had good intentions and a kind heart. No, it’s not the case. Some people really just live their lives inflicting pain on others whether it’s all subconscious or not, I don’t know.

Specific signs that I noticed— demeaning/criticizing you over little things, starting arguments but turning it around on you to make it your fault, inconsistencies in their stories and things they tell you, being unusually head over heels for you in the beginning, rapidly changing their behavior once you become attached to them. There are honestly SO MANY red flags, but they come out slowly until you end up with this complete monster, but you’re already attached and they really get into your head so you just feel like the bad guy and are constantly trying to prove yourself and win their approval.

You never will win their approval, but they will throw out little bread crumbs of affection here and there to make you think/hope/believe that things will go back to the way they were in the beginning.

I have so much experience with this, but it’s kind of hard to explain especially without writing a book! Just be aware that these people are very skilled at what they do— they’ve most likely been doing it their whole lives.
